Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Reza
Message:
fix(A-02): make the dev OTP bypass an explicit opt-in (P1)

server/auth.js: PAYESH_DEV_OTP_BYPASS === '1' is now the ONLY value that
enables the 0000 bypass. Unset, empty, 0, false, true, yes or any other
string keeps it OFF, and NODE_ENV/PAYESH_ENV=production always overrides.
The old predicate (!IS_PROD && !== '0') left the door open in EVERY
non-production deployment, including real servers with a DATABASE_URL.

- tests/a02-dev-otp-bypass.js: 11 mission cases x 2 independent signals
  (send-code demo_code + login with 0000), fresh module per case, plus
  A02_MUTATE=VULN: the pre-fix predicate makes 14 assertions red, the
  fixed one 25 green.
- tests/p11-phone-auth.js: the DEV OTP block now opts in explicitly and
  greps for the new predicate.
- CI: wired the suite and its mutation as an expect-to-fail step so a dead
  negative proof fails the build.
- docs/DEPLOY.md + CONFIGURATION_REFERENCE.md: DATABASE_URL,
  PAYESH_DEV_OTP_BYPASS and PAYESH_OTP_PEPPER documented; go-live checklist
  item 1b added.
- tools/docs-stats-sync.js: hash LF-normalised text instead of raw on-disk
  bytes (a stale Windows CRLF working tree rewrote all 457 freeze rows).
- regenerated doc counts (640 tests) + rc44 freeze manifest.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Reza
Message:
B-PG: bound PostgreSQL blackhole latency and mid-migration crash recovery

B-PG-1a (server/db.js): both pg.Pool instances now carry
connectionTimeoutMillis (PG_TIMEOUT_MS/PG_TIMEOUT, 3000), query_timeout
(PAYESH_PG_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS, 10000) and keepAlive. db.ping()/healthCheck()
probe with an explicit query_timeout (PAYESH_PG_PING_TIMEOUT_MS, 2000).
Previously a frozen connection hung /api/health and /api/readiness forever.

B-PG-1b (server/infrastructure/phase6-canary-engine.js): refreshCacheFromPg()
runs in the onRequest hot path of every HTTP request. _sotCacheAt was written
but never read, so the TTL gate was dead code and each request paid a
synchronous SELECT before route dispatch — the second ~3000ms under a
blackhole. Added a real freshness gate (PAYESH_CANARY_SOT_TTL_MS, 2000) plus
an outage backoff (PAYESH_CANARY_SOT_BACKOFF_MS, 30000) on the read path only;
every authority write invalidates the cache and refreshes with force:true, so
the gates bound read staleness and never block a fail-closed write.

B-PG-2 (tests/b-pg-health-blackhole.js): two-tree TCP-blackhole probe.
Fixed: 11/11 pass, exit 0 — 0 hangs, slowest 6022ms, median ~3011ms, every
response ok:false/HTTP 503 (the endpoint reports its own outage), recovery to
200 OK. Legacy (all timeout knobs off, incl. PG_TIMEOUT_MS=0): 8/8 hang,
exit 1.

B-PG-3 (tests/b-pg-migration-midflight-kill.js): two-tree probe killing the
backend between migration 012's committed partition swap and its ledger INSERT
on the pg-client path (host has no psql binary). Fixed: 9/9 pass, exit 0 —
rerun detects 012's ALREADY_APPLIED guard and records the ledger row with a
matching checksum. Legacy: detection was gated on usePsql, so a psql-absent
host could not recover; RED reproduced, exit 1.

Also updates the stale task-5 assertion in tests/data-integrity-occ-migration.js
to bind the post-D-4 detection shape instead of the removed usePsql gate.

Evidence: npm test 547/547 exit 0; eslint 0 errors on all changed files.
See docs/PREQUISITES.md 133 and Lessons 22-23.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: rezaa2544
Message:
perf(p1-1): users(phone) expression index + auth lookup from PG

Wave 18 §۵-۴: send-code/login resolved the user with a linear scan of
the in-memory mirror (store.users.find). Two problems: (a) at national
scale (10M users) that scan costs ~100ms+ per auth request on the hot
path; (b) in PG-live mode the mirror is hydration-capped, so a user
beyond the cap simply cannot log in even though PG has them.

Change (server/auth.js, userByPhone):
- PG-live: indexed lookup via migration 010 — an expression index on
  right(regexp_replace(phone,'[\s\-()]','','g'), 10), the exact
  normalization key the code already used. Tie-break preserved: ORDER BY
  id LIMIT 1 matches find() over the id-ordered mirror (hydration is
  ORDER BY id).
- "absent in PG = absent": PG is the authority in PG-live mode; only a
  connection/query error degrades to the mirror scan (logged), never a
  clean miss.
- File/demo mode (no PG): unchanged linear scan of the mirror.

Migration 010 (+down): CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS — 007 pattern,
idempotent, data untouched. Users beyond the hydration cap can now log
in (the acceptance test for this fix).

Tests:
- tests/p11-phone-auth.js (unit, 17/17): file-mode dirty-phone lookup,
  enumeration-safe unknown phone, PG-only user with an EMPTY mirror
  (auth from PG, not the mirror), absent-in-PG contract, tie-break
  (smallest id, same as find), pg-mem degrade (regexp_replace missing →
  fallback, no crash), index-expression/query consistency.
- tests/p11-phone-auth-live.js (live PG, 11/11): migration chain
  001..010 on an empty DB, index in catalog, dirty/tie lookups, EXPLAIN
  shows Index Scan (no Seq Scan), down/re-apply round-trip on a DB with
  data, and a full send-code→login for a PG-only user against an empty
  mirror. Self-skips without P11_LIVE_PG.
- Mutation battery M1..M4 all killed (M4 lesson: the assertion must
  check the SQL string itself, not a substring that also appears in a
  comment).
- tests/bench-phone-lookup-p11.js: before/after on 1,000,000 seeded
  users — linear mirror scan (worst case, target at array end) mean
  132.5ms / p95 147.9ms vs indexed lookup mean 0.36ms / p95 0.47ms
  (~369x). Planner: Limit over Index Scan, cost 8.45.

Regression on this tree: smoke 547/547 · otp-ratelimit PASS ·
otp-ratelimit-mutations PASS · wave5-authz PASS · bgsync PASS ·
secret-scan 11/11. authz-model 255/256 — the single red (t_depth /
wave14-observability) is pre-existing on main (verified on a stashed
tree) and out of scope here.

Author: Arena 4 (Wave 18 load testing)
Message:
feat(load-test): implement national load testing scenarios

ابزارِ اجرایِ واقعیِ آزمونِ بارِ ملی روی استیجینگ:

- infra/wave18-loadtest/staging-bootstrap.sh — شش گامِ idempotent:
  PostgreSQL 17 → initdb → نقش/پایگاه → migrationها (۹۰ جدول) → دیتاست →
  api.env.
- infra/wave18-loadtest/run-scenarios.sh — چهار سناریویِ بار + soak پشتِ
  سرِ هم.
- tools/wave18-load-to-pg.js — بارگذارِ CSV→PG با گزارشِ واگرایی.
  deriveEnrollments ردیف‌هایِ enrollments را از attendance×classes
  استنتاج می‌کند: مولدِ دیتاست هیچ enrollments تولید نمی‌کند (۰ ردیف) در
  حالی که server/policy.js برایِ هر نوشتنِ teacher-scoped یک ردیف می‌خواهد
  و بی‌آن همهٔ نوشتن‌ها out_of_scope رد می‌شدند.
- tools/wave18-summarize-results.py — جدولِ سنجه از --summary-export تا
  اعدادِ گزارش دستی کپی نشوند. ساختارِ واقعیِ k6 v2: metric صاف، میانه با
  کلیدِ med، و thresholds که true یعنی رد شده.
- tests/performance/results/w18-*.json — خروجیِ خامِ پنج سناریو.
- tests/secret-scan.js — منطقِ استثناهایِ hex به تابعِ نام‌دارِ hexAllowed()
  منتقل شد تا حلقهٔ اسکن و کنترلِ منفی همان کد را اجرا کنند؛ به‌علاوهٔ
  کنترلِ منفیِ ۱۴ موردی. شش sha256 در stats.json دیتاست، hashِ خودِ
  CSVها هستند (۶/۶ با hashِ واقعی تطبیق داده شد) و T7d در

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: arena-agent
Message:
test: delta hardening gate suites — 19 + 13 + 14 + 18, all green

- tests/delta-sync-hardening.js (19/19): the phase-2 gate — gap 1
  (forced-full flags, boundary, env override, tombstones), gap 2 (cursor
  round-trip, expiry 401, tamper 401, token-wins-over-claim, disabled
  server, TTL clamp/future-iat/jti, client store+send+one-shot renewal,
  replace-on-forced-full), gap 4 (two parallel clients => one
  conflict_preserved + counter; detection-time histogram for conflict
  and clean; exposition), gap 3 (DRY_RUN contract, --live fail-closed
  without DATABASE_URL).
- tests/wave4-sync-all-collections.js (13/13): the delta path swept
  across ALL 19 pull collections — per-collection delta correctness,
  forced-full across the board, subset/fail-closed collection filter,
  tenant isolation (with the documented public/user-scoped exceptions),
  PG-mode builder-per-collection + per-table fallback, no delta SQL on
  forced-full, cursor across all collections, response shape.
- tests/wave10-query-audit.js (14/14): every SQL surface of the delta/
  paged reads audited — allowlist == pull collections, since/keyset/
  LIMIT bound as parameters (no literals), hostile identifiers rejected,
  stable (updated_at,id) ORDER BY everywhere, hostile search lands in
  params not SQL (students/users), composite date|id cursor + legacy
  degrade, LIMIT+1 always bound, source audit of pull.js/syncdelta.js.
- tests/contract-layers.js (18/18): the server<->client wire contract
  pinned layer by layer — transport (200/401 codes), envelope (keys/
  types, unknown params ignored), semantics (delta/full truth table),
  payload (subset, tombstone shape), cursor (issue/absence, distinct 401
  codes, authenticated since wins, cursor anchored at server_time),
  push (results[] uid/ok, conflict row shape, per-op rejection), legacy
  compatibility (plain-since client unchanged; both raw and plain API
  shapes normalized).
